title: am / is / are - forms of the verb to be
shortExplanation: I am, he is, they are
longExplanation:
to be is the most important verb in the English language, an analogue of the 
Three forms: am - only with I; is - with he, she, it; are - with you, we, they.
formation: I am, he is, they are

title: Negation: am not / isn't / aren't
shortExplanation: I'm not tired. He isn't here. They aren't ready.
longExplanation:
Negation is constructed by adding not: am not, is not, are not.
Short forms: isn't (= is not), aren't (= are not). Only am not is not reduced to amn't - an exception!
formation: I'm not tired. He isn't here. They aren't ready.

title: Questions with to be: Am I? / Is she? / Are they?
shortExplanation: Is she a teacher? Are you cold? Am I late?
longExplanation:
In questions, the verb to be is placed before the subject: She is → Is she?
Special questions: question word + to be + subject: Where is he? What is this?
Short answers: Yes, I am. / No, she isn't
formation: Is she a teacher? Are you cold? Am I late?

title: Short answers: Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.
shortExplanation: Only full form - not allowed: "Yes, I'm"
longExplanation:
In short answers the pronoun + to be. You cannot shorten the form of the verb in an affirmative answer.
Are you tired? — Yes, I am.✓    Yes, I'm. ✗
formation: Only full form - not allowed: "Yes, I'm"

examples.sentence: Is she ready? — Yes, she is.
Are they your friends? — No, they aren't.

title: Article a / an - indefinite
shortExplanation: a dog, an apple, an hour, a university
longExplanation:
a and an are the indefinite article, placed before the first mentioned object in the singular.
The choice depends on the sound, not the letter:
• a - before the consonant sound: a book, a car, a university [ju...]
• an - before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour [aʊ...], an honest man
formation: a dog, an apple, an hour, a university

examples.sentence: I saw a cat in the garden.
examples.translation: I saw a cat in the garden.

title: Article the - definite
shortExplanation: the sun, the door, the book on the table
longExplanation:
the is used when the speaker and listener know what they are talking about.
When we put the:
1. The subject has already been mentioned:I saw a cat. The cat was black.
2. One of a kind: the sun, the moon, the earth
3. It is clear from the context: Close the window, please.
4. Superlative: the best, the biggest
formation: the sun, the door, the book on the table

examples.sentence: The film we saw was amazing.
examples.translation: The movie we watched was amazing.

title: Zero article - when the article is not needed
shortExplanation: I like music. She plays tennis. He is from Russia.
longExplanation:
The article is not placed before:
• Proper names: John, London, Russia
• Languages and nationalities: English, 
• Sports and games: football, chess
• Food/drinks in a general sense: I love coffee
• Abstract concepts in general: Life is short. Love is blind.
• Plural in the general sense: Dogs are friendly.
formation: I like music. She plays tennis. He is from Russia.

title: Present Simple - affirmative sentences
shortExplanation: I work. He works. She goes. It runs.
longExplanation:
Present Simple is used for: habits and regular actions, facts and general truths, schedules.
Formula: I/you/we/they + infinitive; he/she/it + infinitive+s/es
Rules for writing endings -s/-es:
• Most verbs: + s → works, plays
• Ending in -o, -ch, -sh, -s, -ss, -x: + es → goes, watches, washes
• End with a consonant + -y: -y → ies → studies, tries
formation: I work. He works. She goes. It runs.

examples.sentence: The Earth goes round the Sun.
examples.translation: The Earth revolves around the Sun.

title: Present Simple - negation: don't / doesn't
shortExplanation: I don't like it. He doesn't like it. (not: he don't)
longExplanation:
Negation is constructed using the auxiliary verb do/does + not:
• I/you/we/they + don't + infinitive
• he/she/it + doesn't + infinitive
formation: I don't like it. He doesn't like it. (not: he don't)

title: Present Simple - questions: Do you? /Does she?
shortExplanation: Do you like pizza? Does he work here? Where do they live?
longExplanation:
Questions: Do/Does + subject + infinitive?
• I/you/we/they: Do you...?
• he/she/it: Does she...?
Special questions: question word + do/does + subject + infinitive:
Where does she live? What do they do?
formation: Do you like pizza? Does he work here? Where do they live?

title: Stative verbs - verbs not used in Continuous
shortExplanation: I know, not: I am knowing. I love, not: I am loving.
longExplanation:
Some verbs describe a state rather than an action - they are not used in Continuous tenses.
Main groups:
• Opinions: know, believe, think, understand, remember, forget
• Feelings: love, hate, like, want, need, prefer
• Perception: see, hear, smell, taste, look
• Being: be, exist, belong, contain, seem, appear
formation: I know, not: I am knowing. I love, not: I am loving.

examples.sentence: I understand you. (не: I am understanding)

title: Personal pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
shortExplanation: You always need an explicit subject - you can't skip I
longExplanation:
Unlike 
In 
Object forms (after a verb or preposition): me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
formation: You always need an explicit subject - you can't skip I

title: Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their
shortExplanation: my book, her car, their house - do not change by number
longExplanation:
Possessive adjectives show ownership and go before the noun.
Important: its (without apostrophe) = ownership; it's (with an apostrophe) = it is.
Do not change in gender and number: my friend / my friends - the same.
formation: my book, her car, their house - do not change by number

title: Plural of nouns
shortExplanation: cats, boxes, knives, children, men, sheep
longExplanation:
Basic rule: add -s.
Special cases:
• -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: + es → boxes, watches, tomatoes
• vowel + -y: + s → boys, days
• consonant + -y: -y → ies → cities, babies
• -f/-fe: → ves → knives, leaves, wives
Irregular: child→children, man→men, woman→women, tooth→teeth, foot→feet, mouse→mice, person→people, fish→fish, sheep→sheep
formation: cats, boxes, knives, children, men, sheep

title: This / that / these / those
longExplanation:
this (this) - singular + next
these (these) - plural + nearby
that (that) - singular + far or already known
those (those) - plural + far
Also used about time: this week (this week), that year (that year).
